routes.description: Establish that contingent reality calls for a noncircular explanation outside the contingent collection and that an automatically actual foundation is a better explanatory terminus than brute contingent reality.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the explanatory demand for contingent reality is warranted, its explanation cannot be another member of the total contingent domain, and necessary or automatic actuality supplies a coherent and relevant stopping point that can rationally move inquiry toward a necessary foundation.

motionBridge.description: Show that contingency reasoning provides a rationally persuasive transition from contingent reality to a necessary or automatically actual foundation, without requiring universal compulsion.

centralBridges.description: Establish that contingent things, including contingent reality considered collectively, are appropriately subject to explanatory inquiry.
Show that the ultimate explanation of the contingent domain cannot be contained wholly within that same domain and therefore requires a noncontingent foundation.
Explain why automatic or necessary actuality removes the distinctive further-explanation demand faced by a merely contingent terminus.
Provide a coherent basis for extending necessity beyond abstract truths to a concrete, potentially immaterial foundation of contingent reality.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Connect the preference for a noncontingent explanation over brute contingency to disciplined explanatory practices used in ordinary and scientific inquiry.
Show that apparent conceivability of a foundation's nonexistence need not establish genuine metaphysical possibility because contradictions may remain inferentially hidden.

routes.description: Establish that explanatory expectations drawn from ordinary contingent objects need not govern reality as a whole and that a brute contingent foundation remains viable because necessity has not been shown to add explanatory value or apply to a concrete foundation.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the demand for an explanation beyond total contingent reality is not established, or if the proposed necessary foundation is no better explained than a brute universe, while the move from foundational or brute status to necessary existence remains unsupported.

motionBridge.description: Show that the argument does not warrant the transition from contingent reality to a necessary or automatically actual foundation because brute foundational reality remains an available alternative.

centralBridges.description: Challenge the extension of local causal and explanatory intuitions to material reality as a whole or to an ultimate temporal and explanatory boundary.
Show that labeling a foundation necessary may redescribe its modal status without explaining why it exists or improving upon brute foundational existence.
Separate modal contingency from dependence so that an ultimate reality could be independent and brute without existing in every possible world.
Require a principled bridge from the intelligibility of necessary logical or mathematical truths to the necessary existence of a concrete foundation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test whether explaining necessary existence through divine supremacy is circular when necessary existence is itself treated as constitutive of supremacy.
Show that distinguishing an immaterial concrete foundation from material objects does not by itself establish that the foundation exists necessarily.
